Lenny was filled with a newfound sense of freedom and joy, and he quickly explored the world around him, soaking in all the new experiences and sensations it had to offer. This condition is often referred to as a "closed" or "hidden" form of spina bifida, as it does not involve an open gap in the spine like other forms of spina bifida.

Symptoms of spina bifida occulta can vary, but many people with this condition do not experience any noticeable symptoms at all. However, some individuals may experience mild symptoms such as:

- Back pain or stiffness
- Muscle weakness or numbness in the legs
- Abnormal reflexes
- Abnormal curvature of the spine (scoliosis)
- Abnormal hair growth or skin lesions over the affected area

In some cases, spina bifida occulta may be associated with other conditions, such as tethered cord syndrome, where the spinal cord becomes attached to the spine and can cause further complications.

Spina bifida occulta is relatively common, affecting approximately 10-20% of the general population. It is often detected during fetal ultrasound or X-rays taken during childhood or adolescence.

- Back pain or stiffness
- Muscle weakness or numbness in the legs
- Abnormal reflexes
- Abnormal curvature of the spine (scoliosis)
- Abnormal hair growth or skin lesions over the affected area

In some cases, spina bifida occulta may be associated with other conditions, such as tethered cord syndrome, where the spinal cord becomes attached to the spine and can cause further complications.

Myhre syndrome is a rare genetic disorder characterized by a range of physical and developmental abnormalities. It is caused by mutations in the SMAD4 gene, which is involved in the TGF-beta signaling pathway. The syndrome is named after the American doctor, Robert Myhre, who first described it in 1971.

The symptoms of Myhre syndrome can vary in severity and may include:

- Short stature
- Intellectual disability
- Distinctive facial features, such as a prominent forehead, a short nose, and a small jaw
- Joint problems, such as hypermobile joints and joint pain
- Skin problems, such as skin tags and skin folds
- Heart defects
- Gastrointestinal problems, such as constipation and bowel obstruction

Myhre syndrome is usually inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, meaning that a single copy of the mutated gene is enough to cause the condition. It is a rare disorder, and the exact prevalence is not well established.
